To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of KBr beam splitters in solar absorption FTIR instruments is a valid alternative to CaF2 beam splitters, (2) the precisions in Xco2 retrieved from FTIR measurements with KBr beam splitter are below 0.25 % and (3) XCO2 measurements with KBr FTIR instruments are useful for the monitoring of CO2 in the troposphere and lower stratosphere.

(i) the precision in XCO2 retrieved with FTIRs using a KBr beam splitter is better than 0.2 %, (ii) the precision is slightly better with a CaF2 splitter, and (iii) the bias in XCO 2 (KBr–CaF2) is +0.14 %.
